column1: # The red run: this tree's assertions against the engine the base ref holds,
# written whole by tests/red, which tests/run --record-assertions calls.
#   base  <ref>  <sha>  <engine version there>
#   run   <failed>  <passed>  <skipped>        lines counted, not the summary
#   <assertion name>  <times it failed>        failed names only
#   an assertion the manifest lists that the base run never reached counts as failed, by its shortfall
# A base of - means no complete red run was made: none was possible, the
# suite stopped before reached or reached no assertion, or tests/red itself
# was stopped; its stdout said which unless it was the one stopped.
# Reproduce with: tests/red <ref>
base
run
a --base that names nothing is refused, not scoped, clean tree or not
a Felix that writes no implicated set fails the job, and a set left from an earlier run does not stand in
a brief that names no file stops at scope: not acted on, not failed, not escalated
a change to the Felix checkout that judges the repair is refused before it judges
a credential written into a file the brief named is red, and is not pushed
a diff felix scope cannot classify is not pushed, and no pull request is labelled
a file the attempt created is outside the brief too, and is not left for anything to read
a gate that cannot be dispatched fails the job
a job runs the gate again only after the repair job pushed
a named file whose name is not ASCII is pushed like any other
a path outside the checkout or inside its .git is never implicated
a pytest test id and a line number followed by a colon both name their file
a repair that changes a file the brief did not name is not pushed, and the gate is not spent on it
a repair that edits a workflow file is not pushed, and the gate is not spent on it
a repair the gate passes is pushed, and says so to the job that runs the gate again
an ignored file the attempt created is outside the brief as well, and is removed
and a brief whose log names no file leaves the set empty
and a run that is no brief empties it, rather than leave the last run's set
and an --implicated file that cannot be written stops repair before any brief
and it dispatches the workflow whose failure started the repair
and it hands that to a person too
and it hands the change to a person on the branch's pull request
and it names the file it will not push
and it names the workflow file it will not push
and it says nothing was compared
and it says the risk rules called the diff red
and its token may dispatch workflows and do nothing else
and lists them in the brief it hands a model
and on the branch the repair pushed to
and passes on GitHub's own reason
and says the pushed commit has no gate verdict
and so when its errors go to /dev/null: the 2 of 2>/dev/null is no second ref
and that output is handed on from the step that pushed, which writes it
and the set it proceeds on is handed on as the step's output
blind allow case 26: update-ref writes refs/heads/backup, and the remote-tracking ref is only the value it reads
blind allow case 27: symbolic-ref with one ref reads it and prints
felix repair writes the files the failing log names where --implicated says
the cloud check is behind the verifier confine
the gate is dispatched on the pushed branch
the gate workflow bootstrap writes can be dispatched
the target of a redirect after that read is a file, not a second ref
the verify step takes the implicated set from the scope step's output, and reads no file for it
with no implicated set from the scope step, nothing is pushed and no pull request is labelled
